title: Investigation on the association of genotype and phenotype in patients with Factor VII-Deficiency
summary:
Factor VII deficiency is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by an increased tendency to bleed.
Factor VII is one of several enzymes (clotting factors) involved in the blood coagulation process. A deficiency can impair clot formation and lead to more frequent or prolonged bleeding episodes.
This condition is usually inherited and therefore often occurs within families. Various mutations in the Factor VII gene can lead to reduced activity of the factor. These mutations vary widely in their effects: while some have minimal or no clinical impact, others are associated with a significantly increased risk of bleeding.
In general, it is difficult to predict the severity of bleeding symptoms based on genetic findings alone. The aim of this study is to explore the relationship between specific genetic mutations and clinical symptoms in more detail. In particular, we seek to determine whether certain mutations are associated with a higher bleeding risk, in order to improve personalized patient care.
The study includes retrospective data from patients who underwent genetic testing between January 2009 and December 2024 and were found to have variants in the Factor VII gene. Bleeding symptoms are assessed using the ISTH Bleeding Assessment Tool (BAT score). In addition, laboratory values such as Factor VII activity (in percent) and other coagulation parameters are evaluated.

interventions.name: Patients with Factor VII-deficiency and confirmed FVII mutation or polymorphism: genotype data will be set in relation to the coagulation status and clinical phenotype of patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with Factor VII mutation or polymorphism confirmed by genetics diagnostic
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients under 18 years
• Patients without confirmed Factor VII mutation or polymorphism
